title: One Index Card Beats Every Budget App

beats.say: Complex budgets always fail you because humans hate math.
beats.visual: A blank paper index card resting on a dark walnut desk under warm side lighting, cinematic macro shot.

beats.say: Here's the fix. Grab a physical index card today.
beats.visual: A hand placing a black pen beside a blank white card on a wooden table, top-down view.

beats.say: Step one. Write down your absolute maximum savings rate.
beats.visual: A hand writing crisp numbers on a card with a black fountain pen, extreme close-up on fingers.

beats.say: Step two. Pick two fixed spending categories you refuse to track.
beats.visual: A minimalist leather wallet and keys sitting next to a blank card, dramatic shadows.

beats.say: Step three. Put a hard cap on your variable weekend spending.
beats.visual: A hand sliding a blank index card into a leather pocket planner, moody soft focus.

beats.say: That's it. No spreadsheets. No fifty dollar apps.
beats.visual: A closed laptop on a minimalist desk with warm amber lamp light filtering through blinds.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions about simplicity.
beats.visual: A single index card propped up against a ceramic coffee mug on a dark concrete counter.

beats.say: Rules you can see every morning actually stick in your brain.
beats.visual: A hand turning off a brass bedside lamp at dawn, cinematic shadows across a nightstand.

beats.say: Because a $5 day habit turns into $226,659 over thirty years.
beats.visual: A lone coin resting on a dark slate surface, moody rim lighting from the side.

beats.say: That wealth isn't built on complex math.
beats.visual: A vintage mechanical desk clock ticking silently in soft focus, dark aesthetic.

beats.say: It's built on boring rules you follow every single day.
beats.visual: A clean wooden desk with a single closed notebook and pen, minimalist aesthetic.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A blank index card sitting under a warm spotlight on a dark wooden table, fading out.

caption: Throw out the spreadsheets. Write your rules on a single card today. #moneyrules #personalfinance #wealth #budgeting #investing
description: Complex budgets fail because they rely on willpower and math. A single index card keeps your financial rules visible and simple.
first_comment: What's the #1 rule currently written on your index card?

facts.claim: $5/day habit equals $226,659 over 30 years invested monthly at 8%
facts.basis: $5/day habit = $1,825/year; invested monthly at 8% for 30 years = $226,659 from fact sheet
